[b]"Krieg ist nichts als die Fortsetzung der Politik mit anderen Mitteln."[/b]

[i]War is nothing but the continuation of politics by other means.
-Carl von Clausewitz[/i]

[spoiler=[b]Logistik[/b]]

In the weeks ahead of Operation Elseyr Eagle the Reichswehr would begin to prepare for its operation to annex Bobian exclaves in the south. Personnel through sealift craft involving both military and civilian ships would be brought in the thousands to the Hochdeutsche Republic of Panesa, the exclave of the Kaiserreich bordering the Bobians. 

From across the border, the troops would be stationed at forward bases including Vorgeschobene Basis Eisen and Vorgeschobener Stützpunkt Seelöwe eventually building up to a force of around 173,000. Logistic hubs, ammunition supply points(ASPs) and fuel farms would be established in Panesa with prepositioned warehouses and depots aiding the logistics efforts. 

Millions of barrels of oil would be taken from strategic reserves in both Panesa and the Kaiserol Strategic Reserve to fuel the tanks and vehicles the Reichswehr would need to use. Fuel pipelines and collapsible bladders would be built or refurbished to prepare the fuel necessary for the war machines. Bulk refueling stations back in Northern Panesa would fuel vehicles en masse, away from Bobian fire, while convoys would bring the fuel south to the fight. 

Roll/on and roll/off craft would become ubiquitous in the Panesan port cities of Monteverde as they unloaded Reichswehr tanks, anti-aircraft weaponry, supplies, food and other necessities. Sleepy Panesan towns would watch as lines of Hochdeutsche armor moved through again just like they had in 1921. Overhead the skies were constantly busy. F-160 cargo aircraft would airlift supplies and troops into Panesa as helicopters ferried troops and equipment around the exclave. Overhead Panesans would also see the J-16s and J-15s as they roared across the skies, running their final exercises before being put into action. 

On June 11th, the Reichswehr had settled on an invasion date. The military would be raised to full combat readiness as the Kaiser called up the reserves and anti-air defenses in the mainland went into full action.[/spoiler] 

[spoiler=[b]Aufklärung, Überwachung und Aufklärung[/b]]

The Kaiserreichs eyes in the skies would help the Reichswehr map out a plan of action. Satellites delivering infrared, SAR and electro-optical imagery would capture Bobian force posture in stunning detail. The Reichswehr satellites would work nonstop locating arms depots, soldiers, bases, aircraft positions, command centers and the other required information. 

Reich Cyberverteidigung, the Kaisers cyber warfare division would work to intercept Bobian communications and probe Bobian cyber defenses for weaknesses. RC-135s would help to map out command and control infrastructure, pinpoint headquarters, radars and air defense systems. The readiness of the Bobian forces would also be watched along with logistics chatter.[/spoiler] 

[spoiler=[b]Aus dem Himmel[/b]]

0300 Hours-Bobian Territory

In the early hours of June 23rd, 2025, the Kaiserreich would begin its assault. EK-70 electronic warfare aircraft would take off from runways in Panesa. Groups of EK-70s deployed from the TKS Ludwigfels stationed 300 kilometers from the coast would move within 100-200 kilometers of their Bobian targets. Remaining in stand off positions, out of enemy range, they would jam Bobian radars to sow confusion and block off vital communications required during battle. They would also disrupt enemy surface-to-air missile systems to help prepare for the ensuing attack. 

The rest of the EK-70s would join the J-16CJ strike groups to provide electronic warfare capabilities to the strike package and disrupt enemy systems as they attempted to engage the strike groups. J-16CJs, J-15E escorts and EK-70s would take off from the TKS Ludwigfels, TKS Adlerklaue and Panesan air bases. At 150 kilometers from their targets, the J-16CJs would fire salvo after salvo of REG-3000 anti-radiation missiles. Locking onto the electronic emissions of Bobian radars and SAMs these missiles would hone in on Bobian AA systems. Learning from the previous engagements with SummitONE, the Reichswehr utilized the REG-3000 because of its LOAL(lock-on after launch) capabilities which would remember the last location of radars allowing them to be struck even if they were switched off. 

Mobile surface-to air systems wouldnt escape the Reichswehr either. The J-16CJs along with the Panesan forward bases release Falkenjagd loiter munition drones. These small, low-flying drones are near undetectable by radar and hard to spot by eye. Electronic signals between operators and the Falkenjagds are nonexistent as well as the Falkenjagd works as an autonomous system. Following launch the Falkenjagds loiter over Bobian airspace until they lock onto radar emissions from Bobian military or anti-air. Once they do they quickly dive onto the target and explode with around 15 kg of force at subsonic cruise speeds. 

At standoff ranges beyond enemy air defenses, the Reichswehr J-16s fire round after round of JSOWs to target Bobian command vehicles, support trucks, fuel convoys and power supplies. This wouldnt be just one strike but a continuous suppression system working towards the destruction of enemy air defenses. Once ISR and unmanned systems had confirmed the success of the SEAD operations the second stage of Operation Elseyr Eagle would begin.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Die Haie des Kaisers[/b]]

0430 Hours-Westlichen Ozean 

Once suppression of the Bobian mainland and exclave had begun, the TKS Ludwigfels and TKS Alderkaule would move to engage the Bobian navy. From the missile cruisers, the Vortexschlange sea skimming hypersonic missiles would be launched toward high value targets including: Bobian aircraft carriers, guided missile cruisers, and destroyers. More conventional anti-ship missiles would also be used in massed attacks by the Kaiserreich navy, intended to overwhelm Bobian defenses. YJ-18 anti-ship missiles used by the carrier strike groups would be launched towards the Bobian craft, focusing more on the escort craft, with the missiles reaching supersonic speeds near impact to minimize the chances of interception. As these missiles flew they would also release chaff to disrupt the radars aboard Bobian ships to confuse them and lower the chances of interception. 

On land Kaiserreich naval batteries would begin to launch their payloads towards the Bobians at sea. The Donnerkeil-5B, a mobile ballistic hypersonic anti-ship missile, would be launched towards the Bobian aircraft carriers in massed salvos. Its range of almost 3,000 miles allows it a wide reach from the Kaiserreichs  mainland. Approaching its targets at near mach 20, the Donnerkeil-5B is known within the Reichswehr as the carrier killer. Naval strike missiles from the naval batteries, launched in dozens from their respective batteries, would execute hundreds of launches against the Bobian forces. 

J/KF-18 naval fighters would take off from the Kaiserreichs supercarriers, armed with an arsenal of anti-ship, anti-aircraft and JDAMs. The J/KF-18s would launch their traditional arsenals of WSM-91 Meereslanze missiles. Each of these would be designed to eject chaff as they approached the fleet, confusing the enemy radars and giving them a greater chance of impacting. The J/KF-18s quicksinks would also be put to work. These JDAMs were specifically designed to explode near the hull allowing them to breach hulls and sink ships.[/spoiler]

[b]Arrival at the Sal-Baliz border[/b]
In the dead of night, the Hydronian army finally arrived at a deserted border outpost in the middle of the desert, the first permanent structure they had seen in days. Due to a previous operation, the border was abandoned by the Sal-Baliz and held by specialist Hydronian forces. It had been like this for months, but the Sal-Baliz gave up attempts to recapture it long ago. The 3rd and 5th desert divisions had put up various defences around both the opening in the border and the occupied settlement of Al-Huduz. The invasion forces have begun refueling and rearming in preparation of the march towards binzali, a large city west of Al-huduz that will allow them to rendezvous with Bobian forces and provide another foothold in Sal-Baliz territory to launch the assault on Aduab from.

May freedom prevail and down with the Sal-Baliz!
